pr_title: Omit unique module versions from canonical repo names
pr_body:
The canonical repository name of a module `rules_foo` is now `rules_foo~` instead of e.g. `rules_foo~1.2.3` if there is only a single version of the module in the entire dep graph. This also applies to overrides, which previously used the canonical repository name `rules_foo~override`.

This improves cacheability of actions across module version changes and also prevents the output base from filling up with outdated module and extension repositories. See the long comment in `ModuleKey#getCanonicalRepoName` for a detailed explanation of why this particular scheme was chosen.

The change includes a bump of the lockfile version as the canonical repo names of label attributes in extension usages are affected.

RELNOTES: The scheme for generating canonical repository names has changed to improve cacheability of actions across dependency version updates. Note that canonical names are not considered to be public API and can change at any time. See https://bazel.build/external/module#repository_names_and_strict_deps for advice on how to avoid hardcoding canonical repository names.

Fixes #20997
pr_comments: @Wyverald @meteorcloudy Could you already take a look at the implementation? If you agree with the new naming scheme and the overall implementation, I would go ahead and fix all the tests.
I fixed all tests except for the distfile setup. I won't make changes to anything other than the bootstrap tests and lockfile patching logic, which I haven't been able to adapt yet.
@Wyverald @meteorcloudy Tests are passing now, I had to update the canonical name of `r_j_e`.
@meteorcloudy I addressed your comment and also added RELNOTES to the PR description.

The changes in this PR have been included in [Bazel 7.1.0 RC1](https://releases.bazel.build/7.1.0/rc1/index.html). Please test out the release candidate and report any issues as soon as possible. If you're using Bazelisk, you can point to the latest RC by setting USE_BAZEL_VERSION=last_rc.
Thanks!

issue_context.title: Usage of bzlmod causes cache invalidations due to module version being in file path
issue_context.body:
### Description of the feature request:


Remove module version from the visible module path as it causes frequent cache invalidations when modules updates. This is particularly problematic in C++ where changes in include paths due to module versions can propagate a cache invalidation over most of the build graph; despite no actual dependent files changing.

review_comments: could pass in the overrides and filter out multiple_version_overrides instead, WDYT? I think that's slightly more intuitive (and realisitically I don't think we'll ever introduce other ways to have multiple versions of a module)

While I agree that this would locally simplify the logic in this function, I think that it would actually become much less obvious why the function behaves as advertised: 

It is pretty clear that omitting the version of a module with a single version in the `depGraph` still results in bijection between module key and repo name. 

If we instead filtered by `multiple_version_override`, we would be coupling the correctness to that (in the context of this function) new concept. For example, what's the effect of a `multiple_version_override` that prescribes a single version (and is that even allowed)? I don't think we'll actually implement https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/17801, but if we were to do anything in that direction, we would also need to remember to update this logic.
`multiple_version_override` doesn't allow less than 2 versions. But anyway, I don't feel too strongly about this, and there's pros and cons either way, so I'm fine with keeping it as is.
